result:
Design pre-registered and validated — `runs/pending_experiment.json` is in place for the harness to pick up. Summary of what I registered as experiment 3:

**Diagnosis.** The two-experiment history points away from architecture and at the training data diet. The baseline's 1993.71 m is ~29% of the map extent (regression-to-the-mean), and experiment 2's classification head was refuted in exactly the way it pre-registered: "features can't separate cells → capacity/training is binding." The training logs show which of the two it is: `train.py` samples 6000 of ~78,000 lattice vantages (~8%) once, freezes a single rotation per crop, and replays those same static images for all 8 epochs — 29 seconds of training. The frozen v2 eval split guarantees every eval viewpoint is 11–17 m from a lattice framing, but the subsample quietly rebuilds the v1 pathology inside the trainable code: the nearest *trained* vantage averages ~44 m away and 92% of the map is never shown to a model whose premise is memorization.

**The one change (category: training).** Replace the load-once static tensor with streaming over a global shuffled permutation of the full lattice — 6000 fresh positions per epoch, no repeats until the lattice is exhausted, a freshly drawn rotation at every visit, crops extracted per minibatch. Architecture, loss, optimizer, batch size, and total step count (48,000 presentations) are all held fixed, so this is a controlled test: same compute, spent on ~48k distinct fresh-rotated vantages (~62% lattice coverage, ~16 m mean eval-to-trained-vantage distance) instead of 6000 static ones seen 8×.

**Prediction.** 1993.71 m → 800–1500 m; success is anything the harness keeps. The refutation signature is equally valuable: if full coverage still scores ~2000 m, training-data scale is exonerated at this compute level and trunk capacity / GAP descriptor pooling becomes the prime suspect — at which point exp 2's head deserves a re-test under this fixed regime.

The implementation brief restates the fixed contracts (exact `train.py` CLI as `loop.sh` invokes it, untouched `model/model.py` and ONNX export, `train_info.json` append semantics) plus memory guardrails (never materialize more than a minibatch as float — the full lattice would be ~15 GB). Wall-time should stay in single-digit minutes on MPS.
